klimit_variant.what: code/klimit/: copies of both canonical adapters and their scoring modules with only the k upper limit changed (128 -> 1000) in the argument checks and the asserts; dependencies copied byte-identical; code/check_klimit.py verifies every copy against its pinned original by SHA-256 and the allowed substitutions
klimit_variant.use: unchanged adapters at k = 10 and 100; k-limit variant at k = 1000, labelled 'k-limit variant'
klimit_variant.label_note: the adapters' reported metadata (max_supported_k=128, requested_k_domain positive-request-through128) is left unchanged by the owner's rule

inputs: GSP e838dfbf... (full-8841823.gsp), u4m index W=4096 positions 06368cee..., queries data/derived/calibration-500.tsv 150917d7..., oracle pinned top-1000 302b63d4... (the adapters truncate it to k; u4m checks use its top-k prefixes)
gates: code/run_i.sh MODE=pre: 500 queries, 1 warm-up + 1 measured round, exact against the oracle: k = 10 and 100: U64 original, U64 k-limit copy, FP32 original, FP32 k-limit copy, u4m; k = 1000: U64 k-limit, FP32 k-limit, u4m. The copies' top.tsv must equal the originals' byte for byte at k = 10 and 100. U64 and u4m must be exact (else the session stops); FP32 is recorded as not exact at a k where it fails and left out of timing there. Peak GPU memory per gate (nvidia-smi peak; adapter torch allocator peak).
gpu_policy: Measurement H rule: code/session_lib_h.sh and code/gpu_holder.cu (copied from exp/arnav/2026-11-23-range-v3-wk @ 5550120, hashes in code/COPIED-FROM.txt): holder working except during our processes, 5-sample clear window, retry every 300 s for up to 12 h; overlapped processes preserved and rerun (at most 3 per slot)

timing.registered: 2026-11-24, before any timing (owner: schedule the run and wait); the launch is automated on cuda5
timing.cells: {GPUSparse U64, GPUSparse FP32 where exact, u4m W=4096} x k in {10, 100, 1000}. U64 and FP32 use the unchanged canonical adapters at k = 10 and 100 and the k-limit variant copies at k = 1000 (labelled 'k-limit variant')
timing.fp32_rule: FP32 is timed at k = 10 or 100 if its gate there was exact and its k-limit copy's output equalled the original byte for byte; at k = 1000 if its k-limit gate was exact and both lower-k byte comparisons were identical; otherwise it is left out at that k and the reason recorded
timing.start_rule: the timing starts only if every gate needed by the timed cells passed and the gate-based estimate including FP32 where exact (analysis/pre.json estimate_minutes.with_fp32_where_exact) is <= 60 min; otherwise it does not start and the owner is asked
timing.design: one cuda5 session (code/run_i.sh MODE=timing); 3 processes per cell, each 500 calibration queries x (3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds), batch 1; within each k the implementations run in rotating order (process round p: the cell list shifted by p)
timing.timing_boundary: as each study defines it: GPUSparse query_wall_ms = query padding and upload through the adapted call, packing, selection, result copy and original-ID mapping, i.e. it includes GPUSparse's Python host path, as in the team's earlier comparisons; u4m query_wall_ms = its C++ host loop (argument packing, launch, result copy, sync)
timing.statistic: per cell: pooled median, p95, p99 over the 3 x 500 per-process query medians; u4m / GPUSparse U64 and u4m / FP32 at the same k: geometric mean of paired (process round p, query) ratios, crossed bootstrap over processes and queries, 10,000 draws, seed 20261126 (analysis/analyze_i.py); peak GPU memory per cell
timing.correctness: every timed output: the adapter's own per-query check against the reference plus its post-timing integer score validation, and compare_topk.py against the oracle prefix (u4m: compare_topk.py); any mismatch stops the session
timing.cross_session_checks: descriptive: GPUSparse U64 at k=10 against the published 6.890 ms and FP32 against 6.008 ms; u4m against Measurement F (0.403 / 0.455 / 0.833 ms)
timing.gpu_policy: as part 1 (Measurement H rule), 12-hour window from the timing launch
